recipes.name: Fresh Green Beans, Fennel, and Feta Cheese
ingredients_raw: 1 fennel bulb, cut into thin slices

steps.text: Fill a saucepan half full with water and bring to a boil. Add the green beans and fennel slices; cook until just beginning to become tender, about 4 minutes. Pour into a colander to drain and run under cold water to stop the cooking process.

Return the empty pan to the stove and set heat to medium. Pour in the olive oil and let it heat for a minute. Return the green beans and fennel to the pan. Season with basil, salt, and pepper; cook and stir until coated and warm. Transfer to a serving dish and toss with feta cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Fresh Green Beans, Fennel, and Feta Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Fresh green beans and fresh fennel, cooked until crisp-tender are then briefly sauteed in extra-virgin olive oil, along with fresh basil and crumbled feta cheese.

review.reviewBody: I am giving this recipe 4 stars with the following modifications. 1. you do not need to boil the vegetables just be sure to cut the fennel thin and add it first to be sure it ends up being tender. You can also use frozen beans. 2. Do not use 1/4 cup of oil, I think it was way too much. 3. 2 min prior to turning off the stove add the basil with sun-dried tomatoes in oil. 4. serve and add feta cheese (a little goes a long way) I just used 2tablespoons. Look forward to making this again!

I'm always looking for great healthy side dishes. This is a winner! Boiling the vegetables softens them nicely . I use very little olive oil to save calories . Think stir fry. Low calorie , great flavor, high nutrients, and even my teenager likes it. Tip: don't tell them it's fennel until they've eaten it.

The fennel, basil, and feta combined perfectly in this dish. The market didn't have green beans, so I used swiss chard instead. I sauted the fennel without boiling it, and it still came out nice and tender. I think this would work well with any green veggie--asparagus, spinach, etc.

I added ground turkey seasoned with salt, pepper, and sauteed with garlic. Then I added this all on top of a bed of penne. The resulting olive oil sauce was very good so I wouldn't decrease the amount of olive oil suggested.

This was my first time cooking with fennel and this was amazing! I added 3 baby bok choys to this in addition to the fennel and green beans since I had some leftover that needed using up. Highly recommend this recipe and will definitely make again!
This recipe was fabulous- can be a side or a full meal. I added two small cloves of fresh garlic and minced onion for added flavor (since I can't have pepper).

I'm new to fennel. I was disappointed when it smelled like licorice because I don't care for licorice. But after it all cooked together, WOW, what a nice surprise! I didn't add the cheese because I'm lactose intolerant, but it didn't even need it. I leave out a star because I wish the recipe had given more information and specifics about chopping the fennel. I went too far up the stalk and it got a bit stringy. With that said, it was totally worth it. I ate over half of the batch for lunch by myself. I will definitely make this again and maybe even to impress someone for a nice dinner!

Great side dish for Thanksgiving or any meal! I tripled the recipe for our large group. Everyone loved this! The flavors work perfectly together and would be a great accompaniment to just about any meat. I had to use 2 skillets due to the amount I made, but it worked out fine. I had to make them a little ahead of time, so after boiling, draining & then tossing with olive oil & sauteing, I transferred to a large baking dish, covered with foil & kept warm in the oven for about 20 min. Just before serving I sprinkled with the basil & feta and it worked out fine. Will definitely make this again!

So easy to prepare, and it tasted as good as it looked. Great way to get your veggies! (I subbed Pam for the olive oil to cut down fat and used dried basil instead of fresh and it was still a total hit.) Will definitely make this again!
really nice blend of spices. cooking the fennel tones down the taste a little. nice blend with basil and feta

I will have to make it a second and third time to really review it well, since I modified it a lot the first time, but I can't wait, because fennel and basil with fresh green beans is WONDERFUL, and the feta cheese was a big hit. I used fennel seed and dried basil, so let me get back to you.....
1/4 c of olive oil was way too much for us. Great easy fresh recipe for any night. Thanks for sharing.
Looks just like thr picture! Love having something different to serve my family to keep eating healthy interesting. Will be making this again.
These were good. I did not have fennel so I would bet they are better with that ingredient. I am going to try this recipe again when I have some.
Very tasty especially for my first recipet with fennel bulb, but I would use less oil next time.
This was my first recipe with fennel. The taste mellowed out a lot with cooking & made this vegetable dish delicious.
